title: What is RepoTunnel
description: Understand the local-first gateway model and what RepoTunnel is designed to control.
searchText: Getting Started RepoTunnel overview Purpose RepoTunnel is a local-first AI workspace gateway. It connects AI clients to the projects and local tools you approve, with separate controls for reading, editing and taking actions. Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard that lets AI applications connect to external tools and data. RepoTunnel acts as an MCP server on your machine: your AI client requests a tool, and RepoTunnel checks the workspace permissions before carrying it out. Core workflow Add or clone a project Choose workspace access and AI mode Start a supported authenticated connection Connect an MCP-compatible AI client Inspect and work through capability-specific tools Verify the result from live project state What RepoTunnel is not RepoTunnel is not a hosted coding environment, a cloud drive, a replacement AI model, or a general unrestricted remote desktop. The desktop app remains the local control plane. Who should use it RepoTunnel is intended for people who want an MCP-compatible AI client to work with real local projects while retaining machine-side control over what is accessible. It is useful for code review, bounded editing, repository investigation, tests, browser workflows and supported device tasks. It is not a replacement for your AI provider, your source-control system, your operating system permissions or your own review of high-impact changes. The minimum setup Install the desktop app, approve one project folder, select a read-only or read-write permission, and start an authenticated connection that your AI client can reach. From the AI client, ask for the registered workspaces. Then try reading a non-sensitive file inside the approved project. That simple round trip verifies both tool discovery and actual filesystem authorization. Start read-only if you only need analysis. Choose AI Review when you want to inspect edits before they touch files. Enable additional device or desktop capabilities independently when needed. Know the limits Linux is the primary live-validated development platform. Windows and macOS releases exist, but native automation coverage and complete process recovery are not identical on every operating system. Review the platform reference for the feature you intend to use. Remote connections depend on an accessible authenticated HTTPS endpoint. RepoTunnel itself does not magically make a local-only service reachable from the public Internet. A guide to the RepoTunnel app Installation overview

Select only the access required for the task, inspect readiness, connect your chosen AI client and verify a small read before expanding the work. Home Use the in-app chat with a selected local model, inspect Gateway and Remote status, and open quick actions for projects, checkpoints, safety scans and Pause AI access. Home walkthrough Projects Add or clone a trusted folder, select it in the project rail and choose read-only/read-write access independently of AI Review/AI Auto. The Projects page also shows framework/dependency setup, project overview and Project Memory. Selecting a file opens the workspace editor with search and editor tools. Projects walkthrough Project Memory GPT Agents GPT Agents is the app’s entry point for Team Mode. Create a persistent two-engineer team for one approved project, supply a goal and success criteria, then copy the separate Engineer A and B kickoffs into their intended AI chats. Follow the shared planning, task ownership, path claims, cross-review and verification stages. Completing a work request keeps the team attached; End Team is a separate human choice. GPT Agents walkthrough Video Video has Projects and Analyze views. Analyze runs Video Intelligence on supported public or approved local media; Projects manages durable production work with scenes, assets, rendering and QA. Choose Transcript focus, Visual focus, Tutorial focus or Full according to the evidence you need. Publication and large optional-tool downloads require their own user decisions. Video walkthrough Analyze a video History History combines pending local review, the selected project’s activity/version timeline and checkpoint management. Pending requests can belong to different approved projects, so check each request’s workspace label; checkpoints can use an all-projects view. Use it to inspect what actually applied, failed or is still waiting. Recovery controls target their documented file scope; they do not reverse arbitrary remote side effects. History walkthrough Checkpoint workflow Checks Choose a project and run Check workflow to inspect end-to-end readiness. The result is Ready, Limited or Blocked and includes a recommended next step. The readiness inspection is read-only. Actual build/test execution is available through Commands. Checks walkthrough Git Inspect the approved repository’s branch, HEAD and staged/unstaged paths, then review diffs and stage explicit files. Commits use already-staged changes. Remote push remains a separately authorized publishing action, including in AI Auto. Git support requires an approved root with its own .git directory. Git walkthrough Connect Manage the local MCP gateway, public provider and optional managed client connection. Configure ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel, Direct HTTPS or the optional Secure MCP Tunnel path as appropriate. The local gateway stays on loopback. Confirm the HTTPS/authentication path and a real tool call before treating an external client as connected. Connect walkthrough Connect ChatGPT Optional Secure MCP Tunnel Commands Use the project selector to work with live one-shot commands, persistent managed processes, launches, browser automation and monitoring. Choose disposable verification when a discovered build/test/check preset is sufficient. Choose a live command or managed process when the work needs persistent project changes or a long-running service. Commands walkthrough Phone Pair and select your Android device locally, choose Off, Limited or Full AI access and manage Pause AI independently. The Phone panel provides live screen/control and supported device capabilities. Permissions, sensitive foreground apps and Android policy remain authoritative. Phone walkthrough HTTPS Setup This screen guides the advanced Direct HTTPS path through local requirements, Internet reachability, hostname/DNS checks and final endpoint verification. Follow the displayed stage results. It requires a working public route and trusted TLS; a hostname alone does not make a private local gateway reachable. HTTPS Setup walkthrough Settings Review runtime diagnostics, startup preferences, signed-update state and local history retention. The current platform’s installation and automation limits still apply. Settings walkthrough Help Use the built-in guidance for projects, AI modes, security, Git and recovery. Shortcut groups cover workspace navigation, the editor and terminal. Help and shortcuts Optional ChatGPT continuation extension RepoTunnel Continuation is a Chromium companion that delivers authorized checkpoints to exact ChatGPT conversations you explicitly save. It is useful for eligible interrupted or long-running work, and it waits for a safe idle chat with an empty composer. The extension source is in extensions/chatgpt-continuation on the project’s main branch. It is loaded unpacked and is not a separate desktop v0.4.1 release asset. Install and use the extension

title: Add your first project
description: Approve a local project without exposing unrelated folders.
searchText: Getting Started Add or clone Use RepoTunnel's local project picker to register an existing project, or use its GitHub workflow to clone a repository into a project location you control. Choose access Read-only: inspection only Read/write + AI Review: writes wait for local approval Read/write + AI Auto: supported writes can apply automatically inside the existing security boundaries Verify Ask the connected AI client to list approved workspaces and inspect the selected project before allowing it to edit. What exactly gets approved A workspace is a real local folder registered by RepoTunnel. The AI uses an opaque workspace identifier instead of receiving an arbitrary host path. RepoTunnel resolves file operations within the approved root and applies protected-path and symlink rules. Choose a normal development folder for your first run. You do not need to approve your entire home directory or an entire disk. Test with a non-destructive request After connecting your MCP client, ask it to list approved workspaces, then inspect the project structure and read a harmless README or source file. Check that the result matches your real project. For a read-only workspace, an attempted write should be refused. For AI Review, file modifications should wait for local approval. For AI Auto, compatible allowed changes may apply immediately and appear in history. Workspace listing works Project tree or file read matches the selected project Protected credential paths remain inaccessible The effective write policy matches what the user selected Avoid confusion with command policy File permissions and command permissions are different. A project may allow reading/writing source files but still require a separate decision for running terminal commands. Inspect both policies when an AI reports a permission refusal. Read the setup panel Projects detects the selected repository’s framework, package manager, dependency readiness and development command. If preparation is needed, inspect the offered setup before using Prepare project. Refresh the panel after dependencies or project configuration change. A detected preview address is a runtime observation, so verify that a service is actually listening before opening it. Open files and save durable context Use the project rail and explorer to select the intended project/file, then use editor or project search for the task. Removing a workspace registration does not delete the project’s contents. Add a useful project summary, goals and settled decisions in the Project continuity panel so another AI can continue with the right context. Project Memory workflow Check the selected project’s readiness Workspace access and AI modes

title: Home and local model chat
description: Learn the Home screen: choose a local model, include project context, opt into safe edits and check gateway and remote connection status.
searchText: Getting Started Home local chat Ollama LM Studio llama.cpp Allow edits What Home provides Home combines an in-app local model conversation with Gateway, Remote and Quick Actions panels. You can ask a question without an approved project, or select a project to give the chat relevant context. The model used by Home runs through a supported local runtime. External ChatGPT and other MCP clients connect separately through Connect; your local model selection does not configure those clients. Choose a reachable local model Start Ollama, LM Studio’s local server or llama.cpp’s server on your machine and make a model available in that runtime. Select a reachable model from Home’s model picker. RepoTunnel discovers models exposed by the three supported local runtimes and refreshes that discovery while the app is running and when it regains focus. Home’s picker lets you choose among reachable models; it does not silently switch to a cloud model when a runtime is unavailable. If Home shows No local model, check that the runtime is running and actually exposes a model. RepoTunnel discovers models already available through the runtime; it does not automatically install or start that runtime. Use the selected model’s real capability information when choosing a task. Download Ollama Ollama quickstart Download LM Studio Start LM Studio’s local server llama.cpp source and server instructions Prepare one runtime before using Home Check the model’s license, download size and hardware needs before downloading. Home discovers an existing local server; it does not install the runtime or silently replace it with a cloud model. Choose one supported runtime and install it from its official site. You do not need all three. In Ollama, download a suitable local model and make sure the local service is running. In LM Studio, download and load a model, open Developer and start the local server. For llama.cpp, follow its server instructions with a compatible local model file. Return to RepoTunnel’s Home screen and select the reachable model. If it is missing, verify the runtime’s server and loaded model before refreshing RepoTunnel. Ask with the right project context Select the intended project before asking about its code. Home can include bounded project context, the current file, a selected code fragment you explicitly add, and an existing diagnostic you attach. Use + Selection or + Error when available. Remove a context chip if it does not belong in the next question. Context may be reduced to fit the selected model, and the chat reports that reduction or a context warning. Start with a specific question about the selected project. Check the context sources returned with the response. Use Shift+Enter for a new line and Enter to send. Stop generation if the request is no longer useful. Opt into edits for one message Allow edits is a per-message choice for a selected project. It enables that message to propose safe project edits through RepoTunnel’s editing and History path; the toggle resets after sending. Keep it off while exploring or asking for an explanation. If you enable it, inspect the resulting change or pending request in History and verify the file contents. Workspace permissions and safe-edit validation still apply. Review an edit in History Understand safe edits Read the connection panels Gateway shows whether the local MCP endpoint is online. Remote shows the configured public endpoint or managed client connection and can open Connect. A running gateway is one layer of the connection. Verify remote work with an authenticated request from the intended AI client against the selected approved project. Connect an external AI client Use Quick Actions Open project registers an existing folder; New project starts the app’s project-creation flow. Create checkpoint saves the selected project’s accessible state, and Safety scan checks its protection status. Pause AI access temporarily blocks MCP workspace access. Resume only when you are ready for those clients to continue. Phone Access has its own local access and pause controls. Save a checkpoint before a large change Choose Phone access Keep conversations organized Home stores local conversations and lets you start a new chat, reopen a recent one or delete a conversation from this device. Switching the selected workspace reloads that workspace’s local conversation context. Deleting a chat and restoring project files are separate operations. Use History when the goal is to recover a file version. Add your first project Connection troubleshooting

title: Connect ChatGPT
description: Connect ChatGPT to RepoTunnel's authenticated MCP endpoint and verify the connection with a real tool call.
searchText: Getting Started connect ChatGPT RepoTunnel Prepare the public connection Start RepoTunnel, approve one project and complete one provider guide. In Connect, wait for Ready and copy the exact public MCP endpoint displayed by the app, including /mcp. ChatGPT’s custom-app controls depend on your plan and workspace policy. Check OpenAI’s current developer-mode guide if the controls below are unavailable; a workspace administrator may need to enable access. ngrok walkthrough Cloudflare walkthrough Direct HTTPS walkthrough OpenAI’s developer mode and MCP apps guide 1 Open the app settings ChatGPT can change labels and availability. Follow the linked current OpenAI guide when your settings differ. Sign in to the ChatGPT account that will use RepoTunnel. Open Settings → Apps and find the developer-mode controls described in OpenAI’s guide. Enable the feature if your account and workspace permit it. Start the custom-app creation flow. Use your own private connection for this computer. 2 Add RepoTunnel and authorize it A public HTTPS response proves reachability only. OAuth authorization and tool discovery must also succeed. Name the app RepoTunnel and paste the exact public MCP endpoint copied from Connect. Choose the OAuth authentication path for this endpoint and continue to the authorization prompt. Confirm the authorization in RepoTunnel’s intended local connection flow. Scan or refresh tools in ChatGPT when prompted. Finish creating the app, then confirm RepoTunnel is available in the chat’s app selector. 3 Verify a real project request Open a new chat, select RepoTunnel and make a read-only request against the one project you approved. Confirm that the response names the intended project and is based on its actual files. List the approved RepoTunnel workspaces, select my test project, and read its README. Do not modify any files. Choose project permissions Inspect the request in History Refresh or reconnect when needed After a RepoTunnel upgrade, use the client’s rescan or refresh flow to load the current tools. Reauthorize if OAuth has expired. A changed provider hostname can require updating or recreating the custom app. The optional continuation extension helps resume saved exact conversations; it is separate from configuring the MCP app. Diagnose connection layers Optional ChatGPT continuation extension

title: Install on Linux
description: Use the official Debian, RPM or AppImage release package for x86_64 Linux.
searchText: Installation Verify the downloaded package Download the package and checksum file from the same official release. Open a terminal in the folder containing your downloaded package and compute its SHA-256 hash. Find that exact filename in RepoTunnel-SHA256SUMS.txt and compare the complete hash. Continue with installation only when they match. For the RPM or AppImage, replace the filename with the actual package you downloaded. A mismatch means the file should be downloaded again from the official release. sha256sum RepoTunnel_0.4.1_amd64.deb Official release SHA-256 checksums GNU SHA-256 command reference Debian / Ubuntu / Linux Mint For Linux Mint, Ubuntu and other Debian-family x64 installations, download the official .deb from the v0.4.1 release and open it using the distribution's package installer. Alternatively, use your distribution's package manager on the downloaded local file. Run this from the folder where you downloaded the .deb. Verify the package name and checksum first. sudo apt install ./RepoTunnel_0.4.1_amd64.deb Official release assets and SHA-256 checksums Fedora / RPM compatible Use the official .rpm package from the release. sudo dnf install ./RepoTunnel-0.4.1-1.x86_64.rpm AppImage The AppImage is a portable Linux x64 option. After verifying the downloaded file, mark the AppImage executable and launch it as your normal user. It should not require exposing the MCP gateway to the network. chmod +x RepoTunnel_0.4.1_amd64.AppImage ./RepoTunnel_0.4.1_amd64.AppImage Terminal sandbox requirement AI terminal/process execution on Linux uses Bubblewrap and is intentionally unavailable if the required sandbox cannot be used. Install Bubblewrap with your distribution package manager if RepoTunnel reports that execution is unavailable. First-run confirmation Open RepoTunnel, confirm it displays its workspace UI, add one disposable development folder and inspect the status of the local gateway. If the UI opens but AI commands are refused, that may be the intended fail-closed sandbox behavior rather than a broken installation. Current platform capability status Add your first project

title: Install on Windows
description: Install RepoTunnel x64 with the official NSIS .exe or MSI package.
searchText: Installation Packages Recommended for most users: RepoTunnel_0.4.1_x64-setup.exe Alternative: RepoTunnel_0.4.1_x64_en-US.msi Official release assets and SHA-256 checksums Security boundary AI command execution uses an AppContainer + Job Object isolation path on Windows. Native UI Automation support exists, but platform-specific runtime behavior should be validated on Windows before making stronger claims. Verify the download Download the official installer and RepoTunnel-SHA256SUMS.txt from the same release. Open PowerShell in the download folder and compute the installer’s SHA-256 hash. Compare the full Hash value with the line for that exact filename in the checksum file. Letter case does not matter; every hexadecimal digit must match before you run the installer. For MSI, replace the filename with RepoTunnel_0.4.1_x64_en-US.msi. If the hash differs, download the package again from the official release. Get-FileHash .\RepoTunnel_0.4.1_x64-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256 Official release SHA-256 checksums Microsoft Get-FileHash reference First launch and permissions Run the official x64 installer you downloaded, then open RepoTunnel from the installed application. Add a local project folder and confirm the intended access policy before connecting an AI client. Windows command isolation uses AppContainer and Job Object boundaries. Workflows that require an AppContainer process to reach an unpackaged local host service via localhost can need additional explicit loopback policy; RepoTunnel does not silently add a system-wide exemption. Platform checks Check the native feature status before relying on accessibility-driven desktop automation or full managed-process reattachment. Package availability is not evidence that every Linux behavior has been validated on Windows. If an operation is blocked by sandbox policy, inspect the explicit error and platform guide rather than disabling operating-system security. Current platform capability status Add your first project

title: Install on macOS
description: Choose the Apple Silicon or Intel DMG and understand the current updater safety gate.
searchText: Installation Choose the correct DMG Apple Silicon: RepoTunnel_0.4.1_aarch64.dmg Intel: RepoTunnel_0.4.1_x64.dmg Official release assets and SHA-256 checksums Updater behavior RepoTunnel supports update discovery on macOS, but in-app update installation is intentionally disabled until replacement/restore safety is verified. Install newer DMGs manually when required. Command isolation The current macOS AI command backend uses the Seatbelt sandbox-exec compatibility path and fails closed when the required sandbox cannot be used. Install the selected DMG Before opening the DMG, download the release’s checksum file and compute the package’s SHA-256 in Terminal from the download folder. Compare the full result with the checksum for that exact filename. Determine whether your Mac uses Apple Silicon or Intel, download the corresponding official DMG, and open the packaged application using normal macOS installation steps. The current macOS command sandbox uses the Seatbelt sandbox-exec compatibility backend. It may not expose the same native automation behavior as the primary Linux development platform. For an Intel Mac, use RepoTunnel_0.4.1_x64.dmg. Continue only when the full hash matches the official checksum file. shasum -a 256 RepoTunnel_0.4.1_aarch64.dmg Official release SHA-256 checksums Updates and recovery RepoTunnel can discover macOS updates, but in-app update installation is intentionally unavailable while verified replace-and-restore safety is incomplete. Follow official release instructions for manual DMG updates. Do not override macOS protections or delete RepoTunnel application data just to troubleshoot an update. Preserving approved workspaces, settings and OAuth state is part of the release contract. Current platform capability status Add your first project

title: Connection options
description: Choose between ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel, Direct HTTPS or the optional OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel.
searchText: Connections Raw MCP stays local The raw MCP gateway binds to loopback. Remote providers forward authenticated traffic to that local service rather than opening the workspace gateway directly to the Internet. Choose a provider ngrok: simplest built-in managed path; uses your ngrok account/authtoken Cloudflare Tunnel: uses your cloudflared runtime, tunnel configuration and hostname Direct HTTPS: advanced self-routed TLS/ACME path OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel: optional official tunnel-client path for environments that use it Set up ngrok Set up Cloudflare Tunnel Set up Direct HTTPS Secure MCP Tunnel guide When a connection is actually healthy A green transport status alone does not prove your AI client can call RepoTunnel. You need the complete path: reachable HTTPS, valid OAuth authorization, MCP tool discovery and a successful tool call against an approved workspace. The raw local gateway listens on loopback. A public provider exposes only the intended remote surface and must not permit arbitrary local file paths or desktop UI access. Choose based on your situation Use managed ngrok for a straightforward public HTTPS path when you have an ngrok account. Use Cloudflare Tunnel if you already operate a configured cloudflared tunnel. Use Direct HTTPS when you control the required public hostname, routing and trusted certificate setup. The optional OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel is a separate transport for environments with official tunnel-client access. These paths are alternatives; you do not need to enable all of them. Where connection setup lives Open Connect to inspect the local Gateway, configure the public provider and manage the optional tunnel-client path. The public-provider panel handles configured endpoints and remote authorization lifecycle. Use HTTPS Setup for the staged advanced Direct HTTPS guidance. When revoking remote access or forgetting a provider, inspect the app’s confirmation and current state; approved local projects are a separate part of the product. Guided Direct HTTPS Optional Secure MCP Tunnel

title: Connect with ngrok
description: Create an ngrok account, find your authtoken, connect RepoTunnel’s built-in provider, and verify HTTPS, OAuth and a real workspace call.
searchText: Connections Before you start ngrok provides the public HTTPS route from your AI client to RepoTunnel on this computer. RepoTunnel integrates ngrok through its Rust SDK and manages the connection itself. You only need your account’s authtoken for this path. RepoTunnel is running and the intended project is approved. You can sign in to your own ngrok account. Your computer can reach ngrok over the internet. Keep RepoTunnel and the computer running while the remote client uses them. ngrok platform Current ngrok plans and limits 1 Create or sign in to your account Open the official account page below. Create your account using an available sign-up option and complete the provider’s account verification. If you already have an account, choose Log in. Create an ngrok account Open the ngrok dashboard ngrok’s public account page, captured 9 October 2026. Complete registration on ngrok; RepoTunnel does not create the account for you. 2 Get your authtoken Once signed in, open Your Authtoken using the direct link below. Copy the token value into RepoTunnel’s local credential field. If the dashboard presents a command containing the token, copy only the token value, not the command. The authtoken authorizes RepoTunnel’s ngrok connection. Complete any sign-in prompts on ngrok itself; keep the token out of chats, screenshots and project files. Sign in to the account whose endpoint and usage limits you want RepoTunnel to use. Open Your Authtoken and copy your own token. Keep RepoTunnel’s Connect screen open for the next step. Your ngrok authtoken 3 Configure RepoTunnel The labels below follow the current app source. Installed releases may show slightly different controls. Open Connect in RepoTunnel and select ngrok in the public-provider selector. Paste the token into ngrok authtoken. Choose Set up & connect. If another provider is configured, use the displayed switch action. Wait until the local gateway is Online and the public connection reports Ready. Copy the exact MCP HTTPS URL displayed by RepoTunnel. Use its /mcp endpoint in the AI client. 4 Verify the public endpoint Open the public connection’s health URL using the same hostname as its MCP URL. The hostname and HTTPS response should match RepoTunnel’s running provider. Then finish OAuth in the AI client and perform a real approved-workspace request. In the following example, replace YOUR-PUBLIC-HOST with the hostname actually shown by RepoTunnel. The health request contains no provider credential. The public provider is Ready and the local gateway is Online. The client completes RepoTunnel OAuth and discovers tools. A list_workspaces call returns the intended approved project. A read-only file request works within that project’s access policy. curl -i https://YOUR-PUBLIC-HOST/health Connect ChatGPT step by step Keep the endpoint working RepoTunnel stores the configured provider state outside the project and attempts to reuse its assigned endpoint across normal restarts. Keep the exact endpoint displayed by the app as your source of truth; account/domain support and provider limits still apply. Use Restart connection when the app’s connection needs attention. If the public hostname actually changes, update the AI client’s endpoint and complete authorization again as needed. ngrok documentation ngrok service status Troubleshoot the failing stage Check the displayed provider error before changing configuration. A provider problem, an expired AI-client authorization and a workspace permission refusal have different fixes. Token refused: reopen Your Authtoken for the intended account and paste its current value locally. Provider or account limit: review ngrok usage and the account’s current plan limits. Gateway Offline: restore the local gateway in RepoTunnel before testing the public route. Provider Ready but client fails: check the exact MCP URL, OAuth authorization and tool discovery. Project operation refused: inspect the project’s access mode and protected-path policy. Connection troubleshooting Workspace access and modes

title: Connect with Cloudflare Tunnel
description: Install cloudflared, create a named Cloudflare Tunnel, route a hostname to RepoTunnel’s local origin, and verify the managed connection.
searchText: Connections What this setup needs The built-in Cloudflare provider uses a named tunnel, a tunnel token and a public hostname. RepoTunnel runs the local cloudflared worker and forwards to its reserved loopback origin. A Cloudflare account and a domain managed through Cloudflare for the published hostname. cloudflared installed on the same computer as RepoTunnel. Permission to create a tunnel and publish its hostname. RepoTunnel running with an approved project. Cloudflare dashboard Official named-tunnel setup 1 Install cloudflared Open Cloudflare’s downloads page, select the correct operating system and CPU architecture, and follow its installation instructions. Install the executable on the computer where RepoTunnel runs. Return to Connect, select Cloudflare and check for cloudflared detected on this computer. If detection still fails, check the installation location and restart RepoTunnel so it sees the updated environment. cloudflared --version Install cloudflared for your platform 2 Create a named tunnel In the current Cloudflare dashboard, open Networking, then Tunnels. Create a tunnel with a recognizable name such as repotunnel-desktop. Select the computer’s operating system and architecture under Setup Environment. The dashboard’s connector instructions include the tunnel credential. Copy the token value from the installation/run command into RepoTunnel’s Cloudflare Tunnel token field. Use RepoTunnel to manage this connection’s worker after installing the executable. Open the Cloudflare dashboard and select the correct account. Go to Networking → Tunnels and choose Create Tunnel. Name the tunnel and create it. Find the tunnel token in the connector’s Install and Run instructions. Keep that token in the local app’s credential field; treat it as a secret. Open Cloudflare Follow Cloudflare’s tunnel walkthrough 3 Publish the localhost origin Select the named tunnel, open Routes and choose Add route, then Published application. Pick a subdomain under a domain you administer. Set Service URL to the HTTP localhost origin reported by RepoTunnel. The current reserved Cloudflare origin is port 43182. This service runs on the same computer as cloudflared; do not use the website preview port, a public hostname, or an arbitrary project development server. Leave the optional Path field empty to forward all of RepoTunnel’s routes, then save the published route. The HTTP hop here is local to the computer; the client-facing hostname uses HTTPS through Cloudflare. http://localhost:43182 Cloudflare’s official tutorial shows Routes → Add route → Published application. Its sample service and path are examples; for RepoTunnel use the localhost origin shown in Connect and leave Path empty. Screenshot from the public tutorial at 2:30, © Cloudflare. 4 Connect from RepoTunnel Open Connect and select Cloudflare. Paste only the named tunnel’s token into Cloudflare Tunnel token. Enter the public hostname as an HTTPS origin: https://YOUR_PUBLIC_HOST, replacing YOUR_PUBLIC_HOST with your published hostname. Do not include /mcp in this field. Choose Set up & connect and wait for the local gateway and public provider to become ready. Copy RepoTunnel’s displayed MCP endpoint for your AI client. 5 Verify and authorize Check the named tunnel’s status in Cloudflare and the provider’s readiness in RepoTunnel. Open the hostname’s /health route, then finish RepoTunnel OAuth and request an approved workspace from the intended AI client. Cloudflare routing and RepoTunnel project permissions are separate boundaries. A successful tunnel does not grant more file, terminal or device access. Replace YOUR_PUBLIC_HOST with the hostname you published in Cloudflare. curl -i https://YOUR_PUBLIC_HOST/health Connect ChatGPT Review project permissions Use a named tunnel for this provider Cloudflare Quick Tunnels create temporary trycloudflare.com addresses. They are a testing path and differ from RepoTunnel’s configured named-tunnel flow. Cloudflare documents changing hostnames, limited concurrent requests and no Server-Sent Events support for Quick Tunnels. Follow the named tunnel and stable hostname setup above for this managed provider. Cloudflare Quick Tunnel limitations Troubleshoot the failing layer cloudflared not detected: verify the executable’s installation and restart the app after environment changes. Tunnel disconnected: inspect the connector status, tunnel token and outbound network access using Cloudflare’s troubleshooting guide. Origin unreachable or 502: check the Service URL, same-machine localhost origin and RepoTunnel gateway status. Unexpected login page: inspect whether an additional Cloudflare Access browser policy is protecting this hostname and whether the MCP client supports it. Health works but tools fail: verify OAuth discovery, authorization and the exact /mcp endpoint. Cloudflare Tunnel troubleshooting RepoTunnel connection troubleshooting

title: Direct HTTPS setup for ChatGPT
description: Set up RepoTunnel Direct HTTPS for ChatGPT local projects on Linux, with routing, hostname and TLS checks, screenshots, provider links and troubleshooting.
searchText: Connections ChatGPT Direct HTTPS setup connect ChatGPT to local files unlimited Direct HTTPS connection usage RepoTunnel HTTPS setup Connect ChatGPT without a monthly tunnel quota Use Direct HTTPS to connect ChatGPT Web to your approved local projects through your own running RepoTunnel endpoint. RepoTunnel adds no monthly tunnel request quota or connection-credit allowance to this connection. This guide covers the network setup and verification. Keep RepoTunnel, the public route and the trusted HTTPS endpoint running while you work. ChatGPT local project workflow Direct HTTPS connection overview Choose the right network path Direct HTTPS puts TLS on your RepoTunnel computer and requires a reachable public route. The documented Linux Mint path uses Route64 and WireGuard for public IPv6, DuckDNS for the hostname, an IPv4-to-IPv6 frontend when needed, and Let’s Encrypt for a trusted certificate. If your ISP already provides usable public IPv6, you may be able to use that route instead of Route64. A router behind CGNAT cannot provide normal inbound public IPv4 simply by adding a forwarding rule. The computer must stay powered on, connected to the internet and running RepoTunnel. Free-service availability and limits are controlled by their providers. Choose a managed provider instead Full project Direct HTTPS reference 1 Check local requirements Open HTTPS Setup in RepoTunnel. Its four stages are Local requirements, Internet connection, Choose a hostname and Finish Direct HTTPS. Start with the reported prerequisite checks. On the documented Linux setup, check WireGuard tools, nftables, OpenSSL, certificate tooling and the system service manager. Use your distribution’s installation instructions for missing components and refresh the screen’s checks. command -v wg command -v wg-quick command -v nft command -v openssl WireGuard installation Certbot installation instructions 2 Create the public IPv6 route If using the documented Route64 path, open its Manager/Portal, create or sign in to your own account, and create a WireGuard tunnel. Choose an appropriate hub and obtain the generated configuration. In RepoTunnel’s Internet connection stage, choose Import WireGuard config and use that configuration. The Linux helper can configure the WireGuard service and port redirect rules; inspect the local privileged prompt and the screen’s result. Keep the generated address prefix, peer values and AllowedIPs as provided. WireGuard private keys belong only in the local configuration. If you configure Linux manually, use an interface name of at most 15 characters, such as rt-direct. Route64 platform Route64 Manager / Portal Route64’s public portal, captured 9 October 2026. The tunnel configuration is obtained inside your own account after signing in. 3 Verify routing and port redirects Confirm that the tunnel interface is active and has the assigned global IPv6 address. For a manual setup using the example interface name rt-direct, the following commands inspect the service and route. The documented public mappings are TCP 443 to RepoTunnel’s HTTPS listener on 43183, and TCP 80 to its ACME listener on 43184. The raw MCP origin on 127.0.0.1:43182 stays loopback-only. Replace rt-direct with your own configured interface name. These commands inspect the setup; the guided import is the setup action. systemctl is-active wg-quick@rt-direct sudo wg show rt-direct ip -6 addr show dev rt-direct sudo nft list table inet repotunnel_direct 4 Create the DuckDNS hostname Open DuckDNS and sign in using an available provider. Add your own unused subdomain and configure its IPv6/AAAA value to the globally routed IPv6 address from your tunnel or ISP. Save the DNS configuration. Enter only your hostname, such as your-name.duckdns.org, in RepoTunnel’s Choose a hostname stage and select Verify hostname. The hostname input is not saved until you choose Configure Direct HTTPS. Open DuckDNS DuckDNS configuration and updates DuckDNS’s signed-out page, captured 9 October 2026. Sign in to create and edit your own subdomain; account tokens are not shown here. 5 Check IPv4 compatibility Some clients need an IPv4 route even when the computer’s origin is IPv6-only. The documented setup uses Netiter’s IPv4-to-IPv6 frontend alongside the hostname’s existing AAAA record. Read the frontend’s current instructions and terms, then set the hostname’s A/IPv4 record to the address it currently publishes. Keep the AAAA record pointing to your real IPv6 origin. Re-run Verify hostname and inspect both IPv6 and IPv4 results. Use the provider’s live address instead of copying a permanently hard-coded IP from an old screenshot. TLS still terminates on your RepoTunnel instance in this documented path. Netiter IPv4 frontend instructions 6 Configure Direct HTTPS A self-signed test certificate confirms local TLS only. It does not establish a trusted remote MCP connection. Return to HTTPS Setup and confirm the public route and hostname checks have passed. Choose Configure Direct HTTPS to save the selected hostname and start the local frontend. Inspect the HTTPS listener, redirect-rule checks and external reachability results. Copy the app’s endpoint only after the trusted HTTPS checks complete. 7 Obtain a trusted certificate Once the public hostname resolves correctly and public TCP 80 reaches the ACME challenge listener, use Get trusted certificate in HTTPS Setup. RepoTunnel’s documented hostname setup performs HTTP-01 validation through public port 80 to local port 43184. Check that TLS certificate becomes Trusted and the HTTPS listener is online. A validation failure needs investigation of DNS, routing, the public port 80 path or the current Certbot error before another attempt. Let’s Encrypt HTTP-01 validation Certbot platform instructions 8 Test health and OAuth discovery Replace your-name.duckdns.org with your own hostname. A health check should return a trusted HTTPS response from RepoTunnel. Check IPv4 and IPv6 separately when both are expected to work. The two OAuth metadata responses must reference the same public hostname and MCP resource that your AI client uses. These requests inspect public discovery endpoints and contain no private token. curl -4 -i https://your-name.duckdns.org/health curl -6 -i https://your-name.duckdns.org/health curl -sS https://your-name.duckdns.org/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp curl -sS https://your-name.duckdns.org/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server 9 Connect the AI client Use the exact HTTPS MCP endpoint displayed by RepoTunnel, complete OAuth, discover tools and perform list_workspaces followed by a permitted project read. A responding /health route alone does not prove the authenticated workspace path. Connect ChatGPT and test an action Understand MCP clients After a reboot or network change Keep the WireGuard service enabled according to the guided setup. After a reboot or Wi-Fi change, check the tunnel’s status, the app’s gateway/provider state and the public health response before asking the AI client to continue. A stable hostname can remain the same while the local network changes, provided the public tunnel, DNS route and provider remain valid. The app’s checks are the evidence of recovery. Connection recovery and diagnostics Fix the specific failed check No global IPv6: inspect the WireGuard import, service, assigned address and peer handshake. Missing IPv4 compatibility: follow the frontend instructions and recheck the hostname’s A record. Certificate validation failure: verify hostname DNS and the public port 80 → 43184 ACME path. TLS EOF or connection refused: inspect the route, redirects, frontend listener and certificate state. Host-header 403: inspect the reverse-proxy configuration; keep the loopback gateway’s Host validation enabled. No actions in the client: confirm OAuth metadata, finish authorization and refresh tool discovery. Canonical routing and troubleshooting reference RepoTunnel connection troubleshooting

title: Optional Secure MCP Tunnel
description: Understand RepoTunnel’s optional OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel transport, local setup requirements, key handling and readiness checks.
searchText: Connections Secure MCP Tunnel tunnel-client Connect When this transport applies RepoTunnel retains an optional integration with OpenAI’s tunnel-client for environments that already use Secure MCP Tunnel. It is a separate connection path from the managed public ngrok, Cloudflare and Direct HTTPS providers. Choose the transport supported by your AI environment. The ordinary public-provider setup does not require this optional tunnel client. Compare connection options OpenAI’s Secure MCP Tunnel guide Prepare the local connection Run RepoTunnel’s local gateway and make the supported tunnel-client available on the machine. Supply the tunnel ID and Runtime API key through the local connection controls. RepoTunnel validates the tunnel ID before starting its managed client. Enter credentials only in the relevant local UI; do not place them in a project, chat transcript or copied example. Understand key handling The Runtime API key is passed only to the tunnel-client child environment and is not stored by RepoTunnel. It is separate from the provider configuration used by ngrok or Cloudflare. A reconnect may require entering it again. Missing availability of this optional client should not be interpreted as failure of every supported connection provider. Verify and stop cleanly Use the client’s health state and then make a real authenticated MCP request against an approved workspace. A launched process alone does not prove that the client can reach the project. Stopping the local gateway also stops the managed tunnel process. Connection troubleshooting should follow the gateway, transport, authentication and workspace layers in order. Verify a connection end to end

title: Workspace access and AI modes
description: Understand the difference between filesystem access and mutation approval policy.
searchText: Projects Access mode Read-only: all writes are rejected Read/write: compatible writes may proceed to the change-policy layer AI Review Supported mutations are prepared and persisted for local Accept/Reject. Stale-file validation is repeated before an approved change is applied. AI Auto Compatible mutations can apply immediately, but project boundaries, protected paths, command sandboxing and explicit Git-push permission remain enforced. Read-only always wins A read-only workspace cannot be modified by AI file tools, regardless of whether the UI currently shows AI Auto or AI Review. The scope of access is the approved workspace, not the entire home folder. Editing policy determines how a permitted write is finalized: AI Review queues a change for human approval, while AI Auto applies compatible changes and records them in history. Validate with a safe test Test in a disposable repository: ask for a read, a proposed change and a current change-history lookup. Inspect whether the action was refused, queued or applied according to your chosen policies. Keep command execution policy separate from file-editing policy. AI Review does not permit remote MCP self-approval of pending actions. History and saved versions Verification commands vs live terminal

title: Large repositories
description: Use RepoTunnel's paged and resumable read tools for very large projects.
searchText: Projects Preferred tools inspect_project_page list_directory_page read_file_range fast_search_files Why cursors matter RepoTunnel ties cursors to relevant source/search state and invalidates them when underlying state changes instead of silently continuing against stale content. A practical exploration sequence Start with list_workspaces and get_workflow_readiness, then inspect_project_page for a paged file tree. Use fast_search_files to locate relevant terms and read_file_range to fetch only the lines you need. This reduces repeated full scans and avoids flooding the AI conversation with generated dependencies and unrelated project files. list_workspaces → get_workflow_readiness → inspect_project_page → fast_search_files → read_file_range What the index excludes Broad scanning honors .gitignore/.ignore and skips dependency, cache, build, symbolic-link and known secret paths. The index is for relevance and performance; access.rs remains the actual filesystem security boundary. An explicit file request is still evaluated against the workspace access guard, even when the index has previously shown that path. Project Memory and live continuity Safe editing and history

title: Project Memory and live continuity
description: Save a project’s goals, decisions and preferences while using live continuity to recover current work without replaying an entire chat.
searchText: Projects Project Memory context continuity goals decisions Open the selected project’s continuity panel Projects includes a Project continuity panel for the selected workspace. It combines saved human context with a current factual resume snapshot. The visible state can show In progress, Needs attention or Ready to continue, alongside current Git state, active or last-completed work and the next step. Save the context another AI needs Choose Add context or Edit context to maintain the project summary, goals, decisions, preferences and next steps. Save the context after making it specific and current. Describe the desired result and the constraints that should survive a new chat. Keep credentials, tokens and private keys out of project context. Goals describe what the project should accomplish. Decisions record choices that are already settled. Preferences capture relevant working conventions. Next steps describe intended follow-up work. Let live facts lead recovery The live snapshot refreshes from recorded activity, Git and managed runtime state. A saved next step is an intention; a completed operation needs a confirmed result. After an interruption, ask the AI to inspect the current continuity/resume state, changes, processes and outstanding blockers before continuing. Avoid repeating an operation simply because an older plan says it was next. Recover with Resume v2 Use the right recovery tool Project Memory keeps context; History and checkpoints recover accessible project files. The optional continuation extension can deliver an authorized checkpoint to an exact saved ChatGPT conversation. These features serve different parts of recovery. Inspect the file state after a restore and the actual runtime state before restarting work. Review saved versions Install the continuation companion Create and restore checkpoints

title: Safe editing and history
description: Use stale-change protection, version history and conservative undo behavior.
searchText: Files & Editing Stale-change protection Before applying prepared text changes, RepoTunnel fingerprints the relevant file state. If another editor changes the file before approval, the old change fails rather than overwriting newer content. Undo coverage Created UTF-8 files when unchanged Full writes and targeted patches Created directories when safe non-recursive deletion remains possible Rename/move when the original path is still free Deleted accessible UTF-8 files when restoration is safe Conservative failures When RepoTunnel cannot confirm a safe rollback or history finalization, it reports failure/ambiguity and retains recovery evidence instead of claiming success. A normal edit lifecycle In AI Review, the model prepares a bounded mutation and RepoTunnel persists a diff/pending action. The human inspects and accepts or rejects it in the desktop UI; the remote MCP client cannot approve its own request. In AI Auto, a compatible write is applied without an additional local confirmation and is recorded with history and recovery state when possible. Read the current file Prepare a bounded edit Revalidate the live file state before finalization Apply or queue according to policy Inspect history and verify final content What Undo does not promise Text edits have conservative recovery rules. RepoTunnel will not overwrite newer content when an earlier edit is undone. Binary deletion and recursive directory removal may be auditable without having a safe automatic undo point. Always check the specific history record before assuming a destructive operation can be reversed. History and saved versions Create and restore checkpoints

title: History and saved versions
description: Use History to review pending AI edits, inspect activity, search saved versions and restore an earlier accessible project state safely.
searchText: Files & Editing History versions pending changes restore undo activity Select the project first The activity and saved-version timeline follows the selected approved project. Choose the intended project in the Projects rail, then inspect its recorded work and local file versions. Pending AI Review changes can span approved projects. Check each request’s workspace name and paths before applying or rejecting it. The Checkpoints manager can also switch between Active project only and All projects; a pending request has not changed the project yet. Review a pending request In AI Review, inspect the request’s workspace label, paths and prepared diff before choosing the local approval or rejection control. RepoTunnel revalidates the live file before applying a prepared text change; another editor’s intervening changes can make that request stale. AI Auto applies compatible changes immediately and records their outcome. Read-only access still blocks writes, and an AI cannot approve its own pending request through MCP. How safe-edit validation works Find the activity you need Search history by the visible record text, select an activity filter and choose newest or oldest first. Load More reveals additional records when the first page is insufficient. The filters include Files, Terminal, Processes, Apps, Browser, Git, Verification, Monitoring and Team. Expand a record to inspect its recorded outcome instead of treating a request or started process as a completed task. Understand versions and request grouping File-changing requests can have a local restore point. When a client supplies a usable request trace, RepoTunnel can group the related mutations into one version. Without that trace, changes remain protected but can be stored as separate versions. Terminal, browser and other activity can appear alongside the file version. Restoring files does not promise to reverse every external side effect recorded in that activity. Return to a saved file state Select Restore this version on the intended saved entry and review the local confirmation. Previous and Next navigate saved version state; Restore original targets the state captured before the first AI edit. Later saved versions remain available after a version restore, so you can return to them. Check the returned result, inspect the project and run the appropriate verification before resuming edits. Compare and restore a checkpoint Run project verification Undo and restore have different scope Undo reverses a supported individual change only while the relevant current contents and paths still allow safe recovery. Version restore targets a saved project-file state. Some destructive operations remain auditable without automatic Undo, including recursive removal or deletion that could not be backed up safely as bounded text. Inspect the specific record’s available recovery controls. Manage retention deliberately Clear All History removes saved versions and activity for that project after local confirmation. Current project files stay as they are, and pending AI Review requests remain available. Use Settings for the configured version-history and checkpoint retention limits. Clearing saved recovery data removes recovery options; it is a separate decision from accepting an edit. History retention and runtime settings

title: Create and restore checkpoints
description: Save a project checkpoint before a large change, compare it with current files, and understand restoration and retention boundaries.
searchText: Files & Editing checkpoint backup compare restore What a checkpoint captures A checkpoint records the project state that RepoTunnel’s AI access layer can safely read. Protected secrets and ignored build/dependency folders are outside that accessible snapshot. Use checkpoints as local recovery points for a selected approved project. They complement Git commits and ordinary file-edit versions; they do not capture the entire machine or every external service. Create one before a large change Choose the correct project, open Home and select Create checkpoint. Wait for RepoTunnel’s saved result, then open History to find the new checkpoint. Give a useful checkpoint a recognizable name. The manager supports renaming and pinning records so an important recovery point is easier to identify. Confirm the selected project before creating the snapshot. Use a name that describes the working state you intend to preserve. Check that the saved record appears before starting the larger task. Compare before restoring In History’s Checkpoints section, select the record and inspect its comparison with the current project. The comparison reports modified files, files added since the checkpoint and files now missing. Search, date grouping and Load More help locate an older checkpoint. Use All projects or Active project only to choose the visible scope, and review the affected paths before approving a restore. Restore and verify the result Restoration requires read/write access to the checkpoint’s project. It returns the AI-accessible files to the captured state, including removing new accessible files created after the checkpoint. Protected and ignored files remain outside that restoration. Select the intended checkpoint, review the affected paths and read the local confirmation. RepoTunnel creates a fresh pre-restore checkpoint first. Inspect the returned restored/removed-file result and run relevant verification before resuming work; running services and remote actions are separate state. Read the History workflow Verify the restored project Delete only the recovery data you intend Deleting one checkpoint removes that recovery point without changing current project files. Clear All Checkpoints uses the manager’s current scope: all approved projects in All projects view or when no project is selected, otherwise the active project. The local confirmation identifies that scope, and clearing includes pinned checkpoints. Check it before confirming. Retention is configured in Settings; protected-file rules remain in force during capture, comparison and restoration. Review retention settings Continuity / Resume v2

title: Verification commands vs live terminal
description: Choose the correct execution surface for testing or real project processes.
searchText: Commands Choose a project in Commands Commands combines the selected project’s live terminal, managed processes, application launcher, browser controls and monitoring. Confirm the project and execution surface before running work. The app exposes command policy separately from file access and AI-change policy. Read-only access and native sandbox requirements still matter; inspect a denial rather than attempting an unrestricted fallback. Run disposable verification Use a discovered build/test/check/lint preset when a temporary copy is sufficient. This path disables networking, bounds execution/output and discards incidental writes after the command. Supported discovery includes safe-named package scripts, Cargo checks/tests/builds, Python test discovery and Go tests/builds. Arbitrary shell strings, deployment/publish commands and development servers are not disposable presets. Run a live one-shot command Use Live terminal for a finite command in the real approved project when the work needs persistent changes or permitted network access. Choose a workspace-relative working directory if the command belongs below the root. Inspect status, duration, exit code and captured output. A nonzero exit or a queued approval is not a successful command result. Start and manage a long-running process Use a managed process for development servers, watchers and background workers. Follow its running/exited/stopped state and incremental logs, then stop or restart the specific process when appropriate. Managed identity/history survives normal MCP/UI reconnects. Full app-restart reattachment is currently advertised on Linux; Windows/macOS remain unavailable until equivalent native recovery is validated. Approve through the local controls The disposable command policy can be review, automatic or disabled. Pending command definitions are rechecked before local approval so a changed script cannot silently replace the one you reviewed. In AI Auto, supported live commands/process starts can execute immediately. In AI Review they follow the applicable command policy and may wait for local Accept/Reject. MCP cannot approve its own pending request. Inspect the application and recorded evidence Use the launcher and managed browser controls for UI verification when the task needs them, then correlate output and monitoring state. Confirm a local preview responds rather than assuming a started server is ready. Pause AI is the emergency boundary for active AI live execution and managed process groups. Keep the result tied to the exact project and runtime you inspected. Run a managed-browser workflow Read activity and file recovery Terminal troubleshooting Checks and project readiness

title: Checks and project readiness
description: Understand the Checks screen, Ready/Limited/Blocked results, and the next step for a project before AI edits, verification or Git work.
searchText: Commands Checks readiness Ready Limited Blocked Check workflow Run a read-only readiness check Open Checks, choose the approved project and select Check workflow. You can run this local inspection before connecting ChatGPT. The check inspects whether the project can support the development sequence. It does not create test files, execute project code, stage files or make a commit. Read the result Ready: the project’s inspection, safe editing, sandbox verification and Git workflow capabilities are available. Limited: inspection works, while one or more later steps need setup or are intentionally unavailable. Blocked: RepoTunnel cannot safely validate the approved workspace. Follow the recommended next step Read each reported item and the Recommended next step rather than relying only on the overall badge. A read-only project, disabled commands, unavailable native sandbox, missing discovered preset or unsupported Git layout can limit the workflow. Fix the specific setup or permission issue locally and select Run again. Keep read-only access when the requested work is inspection; a Limited result can accurately describe that intentional choice. Choose project permissions Diagnose command execution Verify the remote path separately Checks shows whether the gateway/client path is connected alongside project readiness. A successful local check does not establish that a remote AI client has authenticated and can call the tools. Use Connect to configure the transport, then verify a real workspace-list or bounded-read request from the client. Set up and verify a connection Move through the development loop Once the required capabilities are ready, inspect the project, prepare the intended change, run an appropriate verification command and inspect Git state. Use Commands for actual build/test/check execution. Return to History for recorded results and file recovery, and to Git when you are ready to review or stage the intended changes. Choose a verification command Inspect Git changes Connection troubleshooting

title: Git workflow
description: Inspect, stage and commit through RepoTunnel's fixed Git capability surface.
searchText: Git & GitHub Inspection Status Diff Branch/upstream Recent commits Mutation safeguards Explicit relative staging paths Symlink/protected/secret-bearing path rejection Staged-state and HEAD revalidation Hooks/GPG signing disabled for controlled commit execution Push Push remains separate from normal in-project autonomy and requires a current explicit human instruction. Inspect before publishing Use RepoTunnel's bounded Git status/diff/log tools. Staging accepts specific project-relative paths, rechecks the live file/index state and blocks protected/secret-bearing content. Committing operates on the exact staged snapshot, not an arbitrary shell command. Use safe restore-to-HEAD only for eligible files and remember that it still passes the normal history/review boundary. Publishing is a separate decision AI Auto permits compatible local edits and commits, but it does not mean the user permanently authorized pushing code. A push must represent the current user's explicit publishing intent and passes a final secret preflight. Avoid broad force/mirror/delete/all/tags pushes through RepoTunnel's controlled flow. If the user has not requested publication, stop at a locally verified commit. Know which repository layouts are supported The approved workspace root must contain its own .git directory. Parent-repository and linked-worktree layouts are rejected because their metadata can live outside the approved root. Restore-to-HEAD is limited to eligible unstaged, non-conflicted tracked text files and uses the safe-editing path. Staged changes are not silently discarded. Inspect GitHub connection state RepoTunnel can broker supported authenticated GitHub work without exposing its credential to the AI shell. A sandboxed command not seeing a token is not proof that GitHub is disconnected. Keep account/security changes local and check the app’s authoritative connection status. GitHub authentication options GitHub: set up Git Install Git History and saved versions Secrets and protected paths

title: Managed browser
description: Run browser verification inside RepoTunnel's managed Chromium-family runtime.
searchText: Browser Capabilities Tabs and navigation Click/type/scroll/reload DOM/text inspection Screenshots Console/network diagnostics Downloads Approved workspace file upload Semantic accessibility snapshots Document-aware state Navigation returns document-generation information so observations can be tied to the intended page rather than an older document. Start with isolated browser state RepoTunnel uses a managed Chromium-family browser runtime rather than assuming that a human’s ordinary browser tab is available to AI. Its browser profiles and tab/session state are controlled by RepoTunnel. Use browser inspection for current DOM, screenshots for visual context, and diagnostics for console/network errors. Navigation receipts bind the observed page to the new document state. Discover an installed automation browser Start the managed session Open a target URL in an owned tab Inspect the page before clicking or typing Verify the result and check diagnostics when needed Install Google Chrome Downloads and uploads Browser uploads may select only an existing file within an approved workspace. Configured downloads are routed into RepoTunnel-owned temporary workspaces, then intentionally kept outputs may be moved into the selected project. Do not treat a downloaded filename as proof that the file finished successfully; inspect the reported download status. Semantic browser actions Checks and project readiness

title: Semantic browser actions
description: Use short-lived accessibility references and mutation receipts instead of stale element assumptions.
searchText: Browser Short-lived refs Semantic element references are bound to the current snapshot/session and are revalidated before a mutation. Sensitive targets are blocked Stale refs fail closed Sequence execution stops on failure Ambiguous mutations If transport is lost after a click/type may have been dispatched, RepoTunnel records an ambiguous outcome and observes current state instead of replaying the action. Find and act on the live page Short-lived semantic element references are tied to the browser session and document state. After a navigation, significant DOM change or failed action, inspect the page again and obtain a new reference instead of reusing an old one. Sensitive input fields are protected. A failure to type a password or payment credential through the semantic path is intentional. How to handle uncertain outcomes A network or helper failure after dispatch may mean a click or type action already changed the remote site. RepoTunnel records a mutation receipt and returns an ambiguous status rather than replaying it. Before repeating a state-changing action, inspect the current page URL, document generation, form values and any resulting confirmation. Retry only when you have evidence that it did not happen. Never interpret ambiguous as failed. An automatic second click could place a duplicate order or submit a form twice. Managed browser Security model

title: AI Workspace
description: Run supported GUI apps in RepoTunnel's isolated virtual desktop.
searchText: Desktop & AI Workspace Use AI Workspace when The AI needs a GUI application but should not interrupt or take over your ordinary desktop session. Session model Shared isolated desktop Per-app appSessionId Ownership/reclaim semantics Window-scoped screenshots/actions No implicit duplicate starts Other AI-owned sessions remain isolated Choose the right control surface AI Workspace uses an isolated desktop for AI-owned application sessions, so the human can continue working in their normal session. Normal Desktop Control is different: it targets permitted applications already running on the human desktop. For browser-driven tasks, use RepoTunnel managed browser automation rather than starting a new Chrome process inside AI Workspace. A reliable GUI workflow Start or reattach to one allowed app session and inspect its windows. Observe the selected window before acting; use a semantic accessibility reference when possible, with window-relative coordinates as a grounded fallback. After important mutations, verify the actual application state. Losing a chat session does not imply the GUI app should be closed or restarted. Keep a stable appSessionId for ownership Avoid spawning duplicate app instances Do not control RepoTunnel itself Avoid password/credential input through protected automation paths Native platform boundaries Linux isolates accessibility through a private AT-SPI environment. Windows UI Automation and macOS Accessibility adapters exist, but native behavior must be verified on those operating systems before making platform-specific claims. Managed browser Platform status

title: Phone Access
description: Connect a selected Android device with explicit capability controls.
searchText: Phone Access modes Off Limited with selected capabilities Full Pause AI as a separate emergency control Transport Wireless Debugging is preferred. Authorized USB can act as fallback for the same selected device. Capabilities Persistent live screen Guarded tap/swipe/key/text Apps and APKs Files Settings Shell/log/network diagnostics Semantic helper actions and bounded transactions Prepare the selected Android device Phone Access works only with a phone selected locally by the human. Wireless Debugging is preferred when authorized, with USB fallback for the same device when supported. The AI receives an opaque target device identity, not a raw adb serial. The bundled Phone Helper provides bounded semantic accessibility actions, but the user must grant Android Accessibility permission on the phone itself. RepoTunnel does not silently turn it on. Android: enable developer options Android: pair over Wi-Fi Pair and confirm the device locally Menu names vary by phone vendor. USB fallback still requires the phone’s local debugging authorization. Pairing and permission changes remain under your control. On the Android phone, enable Developer options. For supported Android 11+ Wi-Fi pairing, put the computer and phone on the same network and open Wireless debugging. Use RepoTunnel’s local Phone pairing controls with the phone’s current pairing details. Pairing details belong in that local flow rather than an AI chat. Select the intended paired phone in RepoTunnel, choose Limited or Full locally and grant only the capabilities you need. If the Phone Helper requests Android Accessibility permission, grant it on the phone yourself. Verify the live screen belongs to the selected device before asking the AI to act. Google’s official Android example shows Wireless debugging and Pair device with pairing code. Device menus can differ by vendor. © Google, CC BY 4.0. Use the least access needed Off blocks AI Phone access; Limited permits individually enabled capabilities; Full exposes the supported set subject to the phone’s own OS and app policy. Pause AI is an independent emergency boundary. MCP cannot pair/select a new device, raise capability grants or unpause Phone Access. These controls remain local to the user. View the live screen when permitted Control input with granted capability Use bounded app/file/settings tools only when enabled Re-check the foreground application before sensitive actions Understand OS denial An Android vendor, profile policy or application may refuse an operation even when Phone Access says Full. That is an OS-level result, not proof that RepoTunnel failed. Inspect the reported error before trying an alternative. Phone privacy and sensitive apps Security model

title: Phone privacy and sensitive apps
description: Understand the non-bypass behavior around payment-sensitive Android applications.
searchText: Phone Foreground protection When a payment-sensitive application is foreground, RepoTunnel blocks AI screen observation, semantic access, raw input, generic shell and relevant diagnostic paths. It does not attempt to bypass the app's security model. User remains authoritative MCP cannot pair/select a phone, grant itself more Phone capabilities or unpause access. Android permissions and device policy remain authoritative. Why payment-sensitive apps are special When a payment-sensitive app is foreground, RepoTunnel blocks AI screen observation, raw input, semantic actions and related bypass paths. The user can leave that app to resume eligible automation. Full Access does not bypass financial-app security boundaries, passwords, OTPs, system permission prompts or device policies. Good verification practice Test input and observation against a non-financial app only. To verify the block, check that RepoTunnel reports access denied without attempting real balances, payments or credential entry. The bundled helper may remain enabled while observation is blocked; an enabled helper does not imply authorization to read a sensitive screen. Phone Access Security model

title: Team Mode workflow
description: Coordinate two AI engineers with enforced ownership and review boundaries.
searchText: Team Mode GPT Agents Team Mode Engineer A Engineer B kickoff success criteria Create a Team from GPT Agents Open GPT Agents in the desktop sidebar and select the approved project. Enter the product goal and one concrete success criterion per line, then create the Team. Copy the separate Engineer A and Engineer B kickoff prompts into the two intended AI chats. They join once and keep their identities until you choose End Team. Keep the project’s access and change policy appropriate for their task. Planning Both AIs join Each posts a concise plan Each creates a distinct initial implementation task Both confirm the split Execution One primary owner per task Task scoped path claims Distinct implementation scopes Explicit handoff when ownership moves Review and completion Other engineer cross-reviews Findings return to the task owner Success criteria are verified with evidence Complete closes the current request, not the persistent Team Split the work before editing A persistent A/B Team does not mean two agents should race through one task. Both engineers join, post plans, create distinct initial implementation tasks, and confirm the split. Only then is parallel implementation unlocked. Each agent owns at most one active implementation task and must hold task scoped path claims for its edits. Shared browser interaction is serialized through an exclusive resource claim. Cross-review and evidence Each engineer implements a meaningful scope. The other engineer reviews it and gives concrete feedback when a defect requires correction. Success criteria are verified with actual test/build/browser evidence. Completing a request closes only that request’s work cycle; the persistent team remains attached until the human chooses to end it. Avoid duplicate work If a task owner is blocked, use a deliberate handoff rather than letting the second agent independently implement the same files. Refresh team status and wait for the other engineer to post their work instead of guessing what they changed. Read the desktop progress view The app shows the current work request, workflow stage, engineer status, task owners/reviewers, verified success criteria and recommended action. It intentionally hides the raw live coordination feed from the main Team screen. Completing the request returns the persistent Team to Ready. Pause is temporary; End Team ends the collaboration. An attached AI can register the next human request into the same Team without new kickoffs. Continuity / Resume v2 Project Memory and live continuity

title: Continuity / Resume v2
description: Resume from current Git, activity and process state instead of stale saved notes.
searchText: Continuity Factual state wins RepoTunnel's resume snapshot prioritizes current Git/process/activity evidence and treats Project Memory as semantic context rather than unquestioned live state. Use after interruption After an MCP reconnect, app restart or chat interruption, inspect the resume snapshot first and continue from the persisted live state rather than restarting already-completed work. Recover facts before intentions Resume v2 considers live Git status, recent activity, managed processes and bounded project context. Saved Project Memory captures useful user decisions, not an authoritative claim that an older task is still open. After a reconnect or interrupted session, inspect the live resume snapshot first. Compare its recent completed operations with current working-tree state before deciding whether any mutation needs repeating. What recovery does not do RepoTunnel cannot detect every way an external chat generation can end, and it should not claim to restart arbitrary conversations invisibly. Its continuation features depend on explicitly supported runtime and client integration. It is safer to report unresolved/ambiguous work than to claim completion from an old memory or duplicate a side-effectful command. Use the app’s Project continuity panel In Projects, inspect the selected workspace’s Current state, active or last-completed work and next step. Add or edit human context when goals or decisions change; factual progress continues updating from activity. Use History for saved file state and the optional extension only for eligible exact-chat delivery. Keep Project Memory useful Install the continuation companion History and saved versions

title: ChatGPT continuation extension
description: Install the optional Chromium continuation extension, save exact ChatGPT chats, understand its status and privacy, and troubleshoot safe delivery.
searchText: Continuity extension RepoTunnel Continuation Chrome Chromium Edge Load unpacked Add current ChatGPT chat What the companion does RepoTunnel Continuation delivers a RepoTunnel-authorized continuation checkpoint to an exact ChatGPT conversation you explicitly save. It helps the supported continuation workflow resume in that chat after a safely completed turn. It is optional. The desktop MCP gateway, project permissions and ordinary AI work do not require the extension. Keep factual Project Memory and Resume v2 state current even when you use the companion. Recover factual project state Get the source folder The extension lives at extensions/chatgpt-continuation in the RepoTunnel repository’s main branch.
